in_text_mentions: tion deficit disorder. Family and social histories were unremarkable. Medications included amphetamine/dextromethorphan and an oral contraceptive. Blood pressure was normal, heart rate 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate 32 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 92% on room air. There was inspiratory stridor, nasal flaring, paradoxical abdominal breathing, and accessory respiratory muscle use. Laboratory data was significant for a white blood cell count of 19,800 per microliter (normal: 4,000–10,000 per microliter). Admission chest radiograph demonstrated subglottic narrowing (Figure 1).
